fp8_scaled_dequantize.explanation: vLLM multiplies in float32 (single rounding, <= 2^-24); reference is float64

int4.note: bit-exact after one float32 cast; also pack/unpack round trip equals vLLM's

mxfp8_e8m0_decode.note: bf16 output of vLLM equals float64 reference rounded to bf16

nvfp4.explanation_any_gs: vLLM float32 double rounding (<= 2*2^-24); reference is float64

bfloat16_values.why: every fp8 e4m3 value has 3 mantissa bits, exactly representable in bfloat16

float32_affine_cancellation.why: MLX affine dequantize computes q*scale + bias with bias = -zp*scale: two float32 roundings of terms up to 15*scale that cancel, so the absolute error is up to 2 * 2^-24 * 15 * scale (= 15 * 2^-23 * scale, the scale of the element's OWN group) even where the exact result is tiny or zero; vLLM's (q-zp)*scale has one rounding

float32_exact.why: mxfp4 / nvfp4 (exactly representable global scales) / int4 / awq: every product is a small-mantissa value times a power of two or a short-mantissa float32; the float32 result is exact, so equality is required

float32_product.why: fp8 * float32 scale: the fp8 value has <= 4 significant bits, so the product has <= 28 bits and is exact in float64; Float(float64 product) and MLX's float32 multiply are the same single correctly rounded result. The matmul-by-identity route only adds exact zeros. Equality is required: a 1-ulp bug must fail
